tree.deep:
The engine, in the order it should be built:

1. FREE LAYER (now): GBP with real job photos + posts, IG/FB organic (3 posts/week from job content), Yellow Pages free listing, review engine (ask EVERY customer, no gating, per ACCC rules; template 4B ready).
2. TRACKING LAYER (before any spend): GA4 + Search Console + GHL attribution fields + offline-conversion wiring so a Google click can be traced to job profit. Jordan tracked EVERYTHING to the ad level; that is the entire reason his ads printed money.
3. PAID LAYER (Phase 8, after money lane): Google search-only per his 3 rules. Budget formula: needed CPL x lead-to-customer rate = cost per customer; customers wanted per day sets the daily budget. Benchmarks from their real data: ~$20/lead, 1-in-5 leads convert, ~$100/customer CAC on a $530-1,300 ticket.
4. CONTENT LAYER (parallel, cheap): the TikTok/media archivers hold every video from jordan.schofield, jamesnlwebster, the_adamhall and davidlist.me, transcribed and searchable. That library shows exactly which hooks worked (job-story before/after, 'we tried to damage the repair', pricing transparency, weekly-numbers posts).

What NOT to do: no paid ads before tracking, no review gating, no fake ratings, no agency retainers, no PMax campaigns (Jordan: search-only converts for trades).

A 10% discount at 20% margin gives away half your profit. Hold the line; walk from bad jobs: the two most profitable projects each year are the two bad ones you turn down.

tree.deep:
The full sales motion, step by step:

1. LEAD IN: website form (photos + details, W1 fires: GHL contact + opportunity + Slack #quotes-in + ack SMS) or phone call. Multi-bathroom leads create one opportunity per bathroom (spec 3.3), ack fires once.
2. FIRST TOUCH (target: 60 seconds for calls, instant SMS for forms): the ack promises the quote within 24 hours. For phone leads use the Surface Care script shape: name, their damage, the method, the promise.
3. QUOTE (within 24h, usually same day): photos reviewed, priced in the quote app from the price book, margin gate checked, PDF generated (itemised card, GST-inclusive, 14-day validity), sent by SMS (email joins after DKIM flip).
4. FOLLOW-UP: nudge at 24h (2C), 48h (2D), expiry at day 15 with win-back (2F/6A). Rejections get the referral ask (2G).
5. ACCEPT: customer replies YES / e-accepts. Deposit request follows (money lane). Stage moves; Make Scenario 1 creates the ServiceM8 job automatically at stage 11 with contact details stripped.

Benchmark funnel (Surface Care record week): 1,900 site visits, 260 quote submissions, 188 quotes sent, 53 signed, ~$57K revenue. Their steady state: ~1,000 quote requests/month, ~20% acceptance, $890 avg job. Your funnel targets from their mined benchmarks: 13% visit-to-lead, 70% lead-to-quote, 28% quote-to-job.

tree.deep:
How a job flows once accepted:

1. Deposit paid (Stripe link or Westpac EFT) and confirmed. ONLY then drag to stage 11.
2. Stage 11 fires Make Scenario 1: SM8 job created under the right category queue, name+address only. Scenario 3 syncs SM8 status changes back to GHL.
3. BOOKING (per the 2026-07-07 plan): office sends the customer an SM8 booking link filtered to the assigned worker's availability; customer self-picks; SM8 auto-schedules and sends confirmation + day-before reminder. The worker NEVER gets the customer's phone number (sub data-leak control); day-of coordination goes through the office or the office-triggered on-my-way SMS.
4. JOB DAY: worker follows the job recipe for that SKU (docs/sop/job-recipes), photographs before/during/after, completes the SM8 checklist. Cure-time rules: coatings need 24-48h before use; the customer gets the aftercare card.
5. COMPLETE: job-complete SMS with balance request (3D), warranty PDF generated in the quote app, SIGNED fresh in the popup (Allan or Marko), delivered WITH the final invoice (ACL time-of-supply requirement).
6. QA: any defect within the first 30-60 days is an application defect; fix fast and photograph the fix. Surface Care turns repair complaints into content and 24-hour goodwill stories.

Surface Care contrast: their 70 subs coordinate dates with customers directly through SM8 two-way SMS from the job card (masked company number). We deliberately do NOT give subs that access; the booking-link flow gives the same customer experience with zero contact leakage. Employees (Phase E2+) CAN get SM8 logins.

tree.deep:
The four phases (full detail in the canonical doc):

E0 NOW: subs do the work. Sign 2-3 partner subs on a written per-SKU card at disciplined rates. This is the #1 unit-economics action available today. Legal gate applies to SIGNING only.

E1 TRAIN (trigger: $25-30k buffer + 6-8 jobs/week for 4 weeks): Marko trains via the supplier (Hawk/ARS) + paid ride-alongs with a top partner sub, then writes the training curriculum as the company standard.

E2 FIRST EMPLOYEES: 1-2 techs hired from Vietnamese/Nepalese communities. Company supplies tools (~$5-8k/kit) + vehicle. Compliance before day 1: VEVO, icare workers comp, award-rate contract, STP payroll in Xero, super 12%. Economics: ~$85-90k fully loaded = ~$180-220/job at 8-10 jobs/week vs $483+ (54-70% of ticket) for a sub. Employees beat subs from ~4-5 jobs/week utilisation.

E3 SCALE: hire in pairs, Marko moves to training + QA. Employee margin at volume: 55-65% vs 25-44% today.

Risk control: never hire into idle payroll (demand trigger first), Marko signs off the first 10 solo jobs, keep the sub network for overflow.

tree.deep:
The money lane for the first jobs (manual, proven SOP):

M1 quote accepted, confirm scope. M2 deposit request (Stripe link or EFT details) with the acceptance reply. M3 deposit confirmed = booking unlocked (only now drag to stage 11). M4 job completes, balance invoice out same day (TAX INVOICE from the quote app, GST shown). M5 payment matched in Xero. M6 sub invoice received, checked against the agreed per-SKU rate. M7 sub paid within 7 days (the recruiting promise). M8 job closed: revenue, sub cost, margin logged on the job sheet.

Automation roadmap: Scenario 4 (Stripe payment event moves Payment Status pipeline) and Scenario 5 (Xero paid trigger for EFT) are designed and gated on two open questions (R1/R2: exact event + metadata carrying the opportunity id). The Oct-2026 card-surcharge ban means the EFT path must stay first-class.

Targets: hold blended margin at 25-30% floor now; partner-sub rate card moves it to 40%+; employees at volume move it to 55%+. Every week report: quotes sent, accepted, revenue, net, margin %, cash buffer vs the $25-30k employee trigger.

tree.deep:
The compliance stack, bottom to top:

1. ACL consumer guarantees (cannot be excluded): due care and skill, fit for purpose, reasonable time. The warranty is IN ADDITION and says so.
2. NSW Home Building Act: statutory warranties (2yr general / 6yr major defects) apply to residential building work and cannot be contracted out. Licensing threshold $5k inc GST per job.
3. The warranty document (generated + signed per job in the quote app): per-material periods, reg 90(4) mandatory text verbatim, provider details, claims address, who-bears-costs, non-exclusion statements.
4. The sub path (gated): sham-contracting protections, SOPA payment law, TPAR reporting, the s15AA review before any signature.
5. The employee path (simpler): award + super + workers comp + VEVO, standard payroll compliance.

Insurance: $10M public liability current. Workers comp becomes mandatory at employee #1 (icare NSW). Tool/vehicle insurance at Phase E2.

personas.verdict: We run 10 production agents on a $6/month VPS with Claude Code and BigQuery. None of them are magic: each replaces one documented human workflow.
findings: The 10: business analyst (Monday brief), social replier, paid-ads auditor, tracking engineer, website auditor, TikTok analytics, DM handler, operations agent (form to job), quote-integrity checker (same-address duplicate pricing), live chat.
First-agent advice: document the workflow on paper first, THEN hand the list to the AI. Do not start with the agent.
Every morning the first thing I check is the agent activity log, not email.
adds: Your first three should be: CEO brief bot, quote-integrity check, social replier. You already beat us on quoting (your quote app runs LOCAL AI: no API bills).

personas.name: David List (build-quality lens)
personas.verdict: Vibe-code the MVP, production-harden what survives. Own your infrastructure: client VPS, not rented platforms.
findings: Prompt injection is the real security risk for business agents: never wire an agent that reads untrusted input to tools that can spend or delete.
n8n (or Make) still wins for production automations: hosted execution, error handling, retry. Claude Code wins for authoring them.
adds: Add a global error-handler route to every Make scenario (you have Slack #automation-errors: good, keep it mandatory)
Never commit secrets; the .secrets/ discipline is right, finish the rotation

tree.deep:
The full stack map:

CUSTOMER-FACING: WordPress theme (server-rendered, Tailwind CDN, no build step) on VentraIP behind Cloudflare. React quote form embedded (assets/quote-form) wired to GHL W1 webhook. Deploy = zip + wp-admin upload + BOTH cache purges (runbook in CLAUDE.md with all known gotchas).

PIPELINE: GHL (CRM, SMS via Twilio BYOT, 15-stage pipeline) > Make (Scenario 1 job creation, Scenario 3 back-sync, 4+5 money pending) > ServiceM8 (jobs, categories, queues) > Slack (quotes-in, automation-errors, + planned bookings-and-operations, sc-quote-accepted equivalents).

LOCAL FLEET (this Mac): cockpit :4317 (board, business map, customer journey, live Clifford/Cleo feeds), quote app :8920 + Netlify (quote/invoice/warranty engine, Supabase sync), TikTok archiver :8317 + media archiver :8318 (competitor intelligence library), lead-gen scripts (sub recruiting), contractor app (sub dispatch PWA, phases 5-6 pending, legal-gated).

AI LAYER (planned, specs ready): 6 ai-employee specs written (pricing researcher, materials validator, competitive intel, trades researcher, maintenance reminder, DM handler) + the CEO brief bot and quote-integrity checker from the Surface Care playbook. Jordan's architecture to copy: data synced out of the CRM into BigQuery, agents query the warehouse, everything logged.

SECURITY: .secrets/ holds live keys (never deploy, never commit). 7 credentials exposed in old commits need rotation. Cloudflare cache rule must keep the logged-in-cookie bypass (the admin-bar-cache incident). Backups + uptime monitoring = Phase 6.

tree.label: Customer Experience
tree.summary: The full journey (lead to repeat) lives on its own tree: open the Customer Journey page. This node holds the cross-cutting rules and the after-job engine (reviews, referrals, win-back).

confirmations.a: Plain, honest, no hype. Never 'written' or 'guarantee' in customer copy. No em-dashes. Promise 24 hours, deliver faster.
Ask EVERY customer (no gating, ACCC rule). Template 4B. Detractors get a personal call from Allan (Decision 7).
$50 referral credit (template 4D).

next: Open /journey for the step-by-step operations tree
After the first 5 jobs: send NPS (4A) 2 hours post-completion, review ask (4B) to promoters and passives alike
Log every customer question you get asked into QUESTIONS.md; the answers become FAQ + template updates

personas.name: James Webster (service-recovery lens)
personas.verdict: A 1-star review from a person who was never a customer came off Google in 24 hours because the owner called, listened and asked politely. Do that.
findings: We call inbound leads in under a minute and customers literally do not know what to say other than thank you. The bar in trades is on the floor: answering the phone IS the differentiation.
adds: Answer or call back inside 60 seconds during business hours; the ack SMS covers you after hours

personas.name: John Dwyer (incentive lens)
personas.verdict: 97% of businesses never give customers an incentive to come back or refer. A real one (your $50 referral) puts you in the 3%.
findings: Wow-factor moments create word of mouth: the signed warranty handed over WITH the invoice is exactly that kind of artifact; nobody else in this trade does it.
adds: Consider a small loyalty credit for repeat customers (Jordan is building one: 20-25% of his business is repeat, targeting 35-40%)

tree.deep:
The experience contract we are building, in the customer's words:

- I sent photos and got a real answer the same day, with a price that did not change later.
- They told me what could NOT be fixed and what the coating will not do. I trusted them more, not less.
- Booking was one tap. I knew who was coming and when. I was told when they were on the way.
- The job finished when they said. I got care instructions and a warranty signed by the owner, with the invoice.
- A week later they asked how it went. When I left a review they thanked me; when my neighbour asked, I got $50 off my next job for the referral.

Every template, automation and SOP exists to make those sentences true. When a step fails, the crisis playbook (CEO.md) applies: acknowledge fast, fix faster, photograph the fix.
